title: Why act as if ai gen making 3d models is new? And let's discuss how astra compare against the established ones (meshy, tripo, rodin, ...)
author: swarmed100
selftext: I'm a bit surprised why everyone on reddit and X is now acting like it's the first time we see ai gen make good 3d models. Many of us already used specialized api's for this before astra's release. How do they compare? Post your experience here

comments.author: No_Drive2275
comments.body: Because for them it is? We have been using 3D-Agent, Meshy, Roding, blendermcp for a long time. They havent. And they are not using, they are just watching demos

comments.author: _Wilbraham
comments.body: Has anyone acted like Astra is new? I've only seen people treating it as better.

comments.author: ObviousPin2271
comments.body: The main problem has been animation quality. 3d mesh quality has been decent for a few months now.

comments.author: MessageSelfdestructs
comments.body:
3D model and animation quality has only really been good for about a year, if not less, though...

But I agree that the uproar about Astra (let alone calling it close to AGI) is ridiculous.

comments.body: I need to know: can astra do something like tripos low poly humanoid models? If so, I‘m quitting my subscription there yesterday.

hey-

for low-poly humanoid specifically, dedicated asset tools still tend to beat general image→3d demos on clean topo + biped auto-rig.

comments.body:
Isn't part of this new, though?

Before Astra you had to plug in MCPs and specialized APIs as you say. Now you can just show Astra a 2D image and it poops out a 3D model, no blender or special APIs required just an image? Seems new to me.

comments.body: La verdad no tengo mucha idea pero dedusco (realmente no se) pero creo porque Astra no solamente hace modelos, no es un modelo de generación en 3D y tiene razonamiento para decidir cosas en el trayecto (dedusco) que los modelos de tripo o meshy, podrían ser IA's que solamente tienen compresión en el 3D(como un modelo de imagen, que solo sabe representar el mundo en base a una imagen) :u pero bueno. Esto me lo saqué del an*, pq no leí otra cosa

comments.author: Square-Yam-3772
comments.body:
it is convenient to have astra crank out 3d models directly and I can see the hype

tripo is still great though. we get clean-ish topology now and the meshes are nicely segmented i.e. clothing pieces are now separate. makes my life so much easier

comments.author: Zenity07
comments.body:
It's a completely different thing. On the one hand you have special models trained for 3D asset generation, on the other hand you have an LLM operating Blender to create meshes "manually". This is like an LLM controlling the pencil tool in a painting program to draw an image (which it can also do), not the same thing as image gen at all.

Beyond just being quite impressive for an LLM, this also creates a lot of new possibilities for cleaner or more unique asset generation. Specialized 3D gen AI will likely always create more detailed assets though.

comments.body: Dumb question. Can Astra do image to 3d model? Is it better then the normal ones? Tripo, hi3d, rhuynan etc...

comments.body:

In another year or so we will have agents that we can interact with intuitively to give code games.  

Gonna be awesome 😆

comments.author: IZKPI
comments.body: The media pushed hype train. Notice how all the youtubers got Astra first.

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body: Meshy and etc makes 3D models with a lot of polygons. Their wireframe looks like a blob of void. Astra makes them from primitives. It's uglier, but much more optimized in every way. Faster to make, faster to render, lesser file size

comments.author: cluracan
comments.body: Those were purpose-built diffusion models. Now a foundation LLM is doing it halfway decently and through a very different mechanism, which suggests a level of innate spatial awareness that we haven't seen before.

comments.author: Yasmin_Zhang
comments.body: If we’re just talking about raw 3D quality, dedicated AI 3D models still win. Astra’s real strength is the workflow.

comments.author: meshy_grab
comments.body:
The main reason it feels like the wider internet is treating **GPT-6 Astra**'s 3D generation as a "groundbreaking first" is purely a matter of **reach vs. specialization**.  


Dedicated 3D AI pipelines like Meshy, Tripo, and Rodin have been used in production by devs and 3D artists for a while. However, when a massive general-purpose LLM suddenly demonstrates the ability to drive CAD, construct scene graphs, or write programmatic Python code inside Blender to output complex, modular 3D environments, it hits mainstream social media (Reddit/X) with a massive audience that never knew specialized 3D generative APIs existed.  


# Dedicated 3D Generators (Meshy, Tripo, Rodin) vs. Astra

The fundamental difference comes down to **Direct Mesh Generation (Specialized APIs)** versus **Code-Driven / Procedural Reasoning (Astra)**:

  


|**Feature / Aspect**|**Dedicated APIs (Meshy, Tripo 3.1, Rodin Gen-2.5)**|**Astra (via Agentic / Blender / Code Integration)**|
|:-|:-|:-|
|**Generation Method**|Diffusion/Transformer native 3D representations (NeRF/Gaussian Splatting $\\rightarrow$ Mesh conversion).|Agentic code generation (executing `bpy` scripts inside Blender or driving CAD primitives).|
|**Asset Type**|Organic forms, intricate sculptures, high-detail PBR character meshes, game props.|Structured scenes, parametric hard-surface blockouts, modular architectural layouts.|
|**Editability & Hierarchy**|Outputs a single monolithic/merged mesh; topology can be messy or require manual retopo pass.|Outputs clean, separate named objects with editable parameters, modifier stacks, and material assignments.|
|**Texture & Surface Detail**|Extremely high-res PBR texture projections and neural surface baking directly on the mesh.|Basic procedural shaders, simple color assignments, or passes via external tools.|
|**Generation Speed**|Fast direct generation (seconds to minutes for a finished textured mesh).|Slower step-by-step agent execution as it plans, scripts, runs, and verifies the 3D scene.|

# Key Takeaways from Comparing Both Workflows

1. **Astra excels at** ***scene structure and editability*****, not raw sculpt quality:** If you ask Astra to build a room or a vehicle, it doesn't give you a baked, multi-million-polygon mesh blob; it writes a script to build 20+ separately named, modular sub-objects (wheels, chassis, doors) in Blender. This makes it incredible for blockouts and parametric editing, but poor for detailed organic sculpts.
2. **Meshy/Tripo/Rodin remain unmatched for** ***production-ready asset generation*****:** When you need high-fidelity characters, stylized props, or dense PBR textures ready to bake into a game engine pipeline, dedicated tools generate vastly superior raw meshes and textures out of the box compared to LLM-scripted geometry.
3. **The Ideal Workflow is Hybrid:** Many devs use Astra to layout scenes, script logic, and build parametric hard-surface frameworks, while pulling high-detail assets and textures generated by Meshy or Tripo directly into those scenes.

>**Workflow Tip:** If you're building or testing pipelines across both workflows and want to pull raw 3D assets (GLB, OBJ, FBX, STL, 3MF) or high-res texture maps from Meshy—including free tier generations or community showcase models—to inspect wireframes in Blender without spending export credits, you can use the free browser extension **MeshyGrab**. It's useful for pulling raw meshes into Blender to verify UVs and topology before deciding which models to use in your scene.
